targets.authors: Lambert JC, Heath S, Even G, Campion D, Sleegers K, Hiltunen M, et al.
targets.title: Genome-wide association study identifies variants at CLU and CR1 associated with Alzheimer’s disease.
targets.evidence_quote: Because the follow-up and replication of GWAS findings provide further validation of proposed signals, we decided to evaluate a CR1 marker with the most consistent association to AD (rs3818361) as a genetic modifying factor for AD risk in a sample of the Spanish population.
targets.outcome_quote: Importantly, the observed effect size and its direction were concordant with previous results [1].
targets.outcome_reasoning: Own Spanish sample was nonsignificant, but authors explicitly compare its effect size and direction as concordant with the original. This comparison supports successful under the author-comparison rule; pooled meta-analysis significance is not used as the replication outcome.

targets.authors: Harold D, Abraham R, Hollingworth P, Sims R, Gerrish A, Hamshere ML, et al.
targets.title: Genome-wide association study identifies variants at CLU and PICALM associated with Alzheimer’s disease.
targets.evidence_quote: Furthermore, a consistent signal within CR1 gene was observed in a concurrent independent GWA study published by other European researchers, although no GWAS significance was achieved in that particular study [2]. Because the follow-up and replication of GWAS findings provide further validation of proposed signals, we decided to evaluate a CR1 marker with the most consistent association to AD (rs3818361) as a genetic modifying factor for AD risk in a sample of the Spanish population.
targets.outcome_quote: Overall, the CR1 rs3818361 marker was not significantly associated to AD in this sample of the Spanish population.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The paper describes this original as a consistent CR1 signal without genome-wide significance; its own sample likewise shows a nonsignificant same-direction trend. Implicit agreement; less certain than the explicit comparison to Lambert. Original data included in meta-analysis do not alone constitute a separate reproduction.

reasoning: Title, author list and DOI verified in the six-page article. New Spanish case-control genotyping retests the CR1 associations from the two introductory GWAS papers. Later replication studies cited to contextualize effect sizes and pooled data sources are not additional independent targets. The meta-analysis is distinguished from the new-sample replication. PDF column order was resolved when transcribing sentences.
